title: Testing what really differs
question: Which differences in attack type, breach size, detection time and regional crime are real rather than chance?

data_in.dataset: VCDB validated incidents and NCRB Crime in India 2024 state tables
prep_steps: Primary action is the single action category, or multiple; unknown dropped for chi-square tests
Action rows with fewer than 5 incidents dropped from contingency tables
Internal vs external compares incidents with only one actor class
States and UTs grouped into five regions by CyCRS (Chhattisgarh in East, Madhya Pradesh in West)
Holm correction applied across all tests in the table

why: Normality checks fail for breach size (internal p 2.1e-42) and for log discovery time (p 3.6e-15), so rank-based tests (Mann-Whitney, Kruskal-Wallis) are primary. Attack type, size and sector are categorical, so association is tested with chi-square and sized with Cramer's V, and ransomware share is a proportion, so a two-proportion z-test fits. Running 9 tests raises the chance of a false alarm, so Holm-adjusted p-values decide.

data_properties.name: Shapiro-Wilk p, log records lost, internal
data_properties.implication: Not normal: use a rank test.

data_properties.name: Levene p, discovery days by sector
Tests rejected after Holm
data_properties.implication: Number of differences treated as real.

alternatives.why_not: Assumes normal data; Shapiro-Wilk rejects normality even after the log transform.

alternatives.model: One-way ANOVA as primary test for discovery time
alternatives.why_not: Normality and equal variance fail (Levene p 1.5e-09); ANOVA is kept only as a comparison row.
Expected counts are large (minimum 0.2), so chi-square is accurate and Fisher is unnecessary.

assumptions.check: Shapiro-Wilk on log records lost, internal actors
Shapiro-Wilk on log records lost, external actors
Levene equal variance, discovery by sector

assumptions.action_taken: Rare action rows dropped before testing.

tables.title: Hypothesis tests
rows: Does the kind of attack depend on business size?
Action category is independent of victim size
Chi-square test of independence
Both variables are categorical (nominal action, size band); 7540 incidents, minimum expected count 1.2
Cramer's V 0.182 (small)
reject H0
Small, medium and large organisations face a different attack mix, so CyCRS weights threats by size.
Does the kind of attack depend on the sector?
Action category is independent of sector
Chi-square test of independence
Both variables are categorical; top 8 sectors, 9061 incidents, minimum expected count 0.2
Cramer's V 0.248 (small)
reject H0
Each sector has its own attack mix, so CyCRS starts from the sector's own threat profile.
Do insiders or outsiders cause bigger breaches?
Records lost has the same distribution for internal and external actors
Mann-Whitney U
Shapiro-Wilk rejects normality even on the log scale (internal p 2.1e-42, external p 7.1e-16), so a rank test replaces the t-test
rank-biserial r 0.516 (large)
reject H0
Breach size differs by who caused it, so insider and outsider threats get different loss estimates.
Do some sectors take longer to notice a breach?
Discovery time has the same distribution in every sector
Kruskal-Wallis H with Dunn post-hoc (Holm)
Shapiro-Wilk rejects normality of log discovery days (p 3.6e-15) and Levene p is 1.5e-09, so the rank-based test is primary
epsilon squared 0.007 (negligible)
do not reject H0
Sectors detect breaches at similar speeds.
Same question, parametric comparison
Mean log discovery time is equal across sectors
One-way ANOVA (comparison only)
Shown to compare with Kruskal-Wallis; its normality assumption fails here
eta squared 0.014 (small)
reject H0
The parametric test agrees that sectors differ.
Has ransomware become more common since 2020?
The share of incidents involving ransomware is the same before and from 2020
Two-proportion z-test
The outcome is binary (ransomware or not) with large samples (1778 and 8818 incidents)
Cohen's h 1.361 (large)
reject H0
Ransomware share moved from 2.4% before 2020 to 55.2% from 2020, so backups and endpoint protection rank higher.
Robustness: has ransomware risen since 2020 without the 2023 batch?
Excluding 2023, the ransomware share is the same before and from 2020
Two-proportion z-test
Same binary outcome with 857 incidents dated 2023 removed, because 91% of them are ransomware and may reflect how VCDB collected that year
Cohen's h 0.666 (medium)
reject H0
Without 2023 the share still moves from 2.4% to 22.1%, so the rise is not only a 2023 collection effect.
Is cyber crime more common in some regions of India?
Mean cyber crime rate per lakh is equal across the five regions
One-way ANOVA with Tukey HSD
Requested parametric comparison of a ratio-scale rate over 36 states and UTs; Shapiro p 9.3e-11 is reported as a caution
eta squared 0.241 (large)
do not reject H0
Regional rate differences are within chance, so region is a weak signal.
Do regions differ in the type of cyber crime?
Crime-type mix is independent of region
Chi-square test of independence
Counts of 101928 cases in 5 crime types by 5 regions
Cramer's V 0.271 (small)
reject H0
The crime mix differs by region, so local crime types are shown to the user.

data.x: Does the kind of attack depend on business size?
Does the kind of attack depend on the sector?
Do insiders or outsiders cause bigger breaches?
Do some sectors take longer to notice a breach?
Has ransomware become more common since 2020?
Robustness: has ransomware risen since 2020 without the 2023 batch?
Is cyber crime more common in some regions of India?
Do regions differ in the type of cyber crime?

yields: 7 of 9 tested differences hold up after correcting for multiple tests: attack mix by business size, attack mix by sector, breach size by insider or outsider, detection time by sector (ANOVA), the rise in ransomware share, the ransomware rise without 2023, crime type mix by Indian region, while detection time by sector (Kruskal-Wallis), crime rate by Indian region could be chance. CyCRS uses only the differences that survive as inputs for tailoring its advice, and shows the effect size so a statistically real but tiny difference is not oversold.
limitations: VCDB is not a random sample of businesses, so tests describe reported incidents.
With thousands of incidents even negligible differences can be significant; read the effect size.
The five-region grouping of states is a CyCRS choice and affects the regional tests.
857 incidents are dated 2023 and 91% of them involve ransomware; without them the share from 2020 is 22.1% instead of 55.2% (robustness row), so part of the rise is a collection effect.
